page: Google Cloud Platform n2-highcpu-4 is an x86_64 architecture server instance belonging to the N2 family. It features 4 dedicated vCPUs powered by an Intel Xeon processor running at 2.8 GHz, consisting of 2 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled. The system is configured with 4.0 GB of RAM, yielding a resource density of 1.0 GB of memory per core. It does not include bundled local storage or GPU hardware. The processor features an L3 cache size of 33 MB, alongside L1d and L2 caches of 32 KB and 1.0 MB respectively, and supports instruction sets such as AVX-512 and AES cryptography.

Benchmark data indicates that the instance generally operates in the lower performance tiers. The stress-ng single-core and multi-core CPU tests place the server in the bottom 25% of benchmarked instances, with scores of 1403.59 and 3699.56 respectively. Memory performance is also constrained, with a PassMark memory score of 1052.97, placing it in the bottom 10%. Large block memory read and write bandwidths are measured at 27.14 GB/sec and 22.64 GB/sec. However, certain workloads show moderate relative performance; the Geekbench single-core score of 1156.0 and text processing score of 1444.0 both fall within the middle 50% average tier.

Given the low memory-to-vCPU ratio of 1:1 and the lack of local storage, this instance is designed for compute-heavy tasks that do not require large memory footprints. It is suitable for basic web serving, light text processing, or single-threaded decompression tasks, as demonstrated by its average bzip3 single-threaded decompression speed of 8.97 GB/sec. It is less suited for memory-intensive database operations, which scored in the bottom 25% on PassMark, or multi-threaded decompression, which fell into the bottom 10%. From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, the dedicated vCPU allocation provides predictable compute performance for lightweight workloads without the overhead of larger memory allocations.
